purpose: Separate threshold recruitment from calling intensification, test whether cross-route species-specific rainfall response heterogeneity can explain the NAAMP allocation, and audit an independent Australian fixed-PAM dataset for matrix-replication eligibility.

calling_index_decomposition.question: Does recent-rain change in calling intensity arise mainly from 0-to-positive recruitment of species x stop cells or from stronger CallingIndex among cells already positive in both surveys?
calling_index_decomposition.sample: Exactly the current 4,236 NAAMP wetter-drier matched pairs and aligned ten stops.
calling_index_decomposition.cell_score: CallingIndex 0,1,2,3; if duplicate Count records occur for the same RunID x StopNumber x Species, use the maximum index and report duplicate/conflict counts.

exact_components.activation: sum wet CallingIndex for cells with dry=0 and wet>0
exact_components.deactivation: negative sum dry CallingIndex for cells with dry>0 and wet=0
exact_components.shared_intensity: sum(wet-dry) for cells positive in both runs
exact_components.total: sum(wet-dry) over all cells; must equal activation + deactivation + shared_intensity

calling_index_decomposition.models: Each pair-level component ~ rain_contrast + temp_difference + doy_difference + year_gap + State + RunNumber, route-clustered covariance, matching the current analysis.
calling_index_decomposition.prediction: Threshold recruitment is supported if activation contributes a positive majority of the total CallingIndex rainfall slope and exceeds the shared-intensity contribution. Shared-intensity is reported regardless of sign; no equivalence claim is authorized.
calling_index_decomposition.interpretation_boundary: CallingIndex is ordinal acoustic intensity, not abundance, mating success, or individual calling effort.

crossfit_species_shift_null.question: Can species-specific rainfall-response shifts learned on different routes reproduce the observed four-component boundary allocation?
crossfit_species_shift_null.split: Deterministic SHA256 split of State:RouteNumber into route folds A/B; learn species response on the opposite fold and apply only to held-out routes.
crossfit_species_shift_null.training_response: For every eligible run x species, number of positive stops out of 10.
crossfit_species_shift_null.training_model: Per-species binomial GLM of stop-positive proportion on log1p(DaysSinceRain), mean temperature, cyclic day of year, State and RunNumber; regularized fallback allowed only for separation. Differential wet shift is minus the learned dryness coefficient. Species not estimable in the opposite fold receive zero differential shift.
crossfit_species_shift_null.test_baseline: Current kappa=2 dry-history species x stop probabilities in the held-out stratum.
crossfit_species_shift_null.pair_shift: q=logit^-1(logit(p_baseline)+gamma_species*rain_contrast+delta_pair), with one common delta_pair solved to match the pair's observed wet incidence count in expectation.
crossfit_species_shift_null.primary_test: Same four-component Mahalanobis omnibus as the current uniform null; Monte Carlo plus-one p.

interpretation.fail_to_reject: Cross-route species-level response heterogeneity is sufficient to reproduce the observed allocation under this null family; do not attribute the residual pattern to site-specific recruitment.
interpretation.reject: Species-level rainfall-response heterogeneity alone is insufficient; additional site or species x site structure is required.

crossfit_species_shift_null.estimability: A species-specific dryness slope is learned only with at least 20 positive stop-cells distributed across at least 5 training routes; otherwise its differential shift is fixed to zero. This rule is fixed before endpoint readback.

australian_fixed_pam_eligibility.source: Hoefer et al. 2026 fixed PAM dataset, GitHub/Zenodo v2.0
australian_fixed_pam_eligibility.design: Six eastern Australian open-eucalypt woodland sites, four fixed plots per site (WetA, WetB, DryA, DryB).
gate: Species detections must retain plot and date.
A plot-day effort frame including zero-frog days must be reconstructable without assuming that missing detection rows imply sampling.
At least three plots must be concurrently sampled on enough days to form a spatial incidence matrix.
Rainfall exposure must be linkable by site/date from a reproducible gridded source.
If effort zeros cannot be reconstructed, no NAAMP-style boundary-replication claim is authorized.

species_vs_site_axis_contrast.question: Is the excess boundary recruitment stronger along the taxonomic axis (route-new species) than along the spatial axis (newly active stops)?
species_vs_site_axis_contrast.statistic: taxonomic_deepening coefficient share minus spatial_spread coefficient share; equivalently route-new boundary share minus new-stop boundary share because corner expansion cancels.
species_vs_site_axis_contrast.observed_reference: Use the frozen four-component NAAMP rainfall coefficients.
nulls: Primary persistence-preserving null at anchor a=0.75.
species_vs_site_axis_contrast.decision: Report the observed contrast, null mean and 95% interval, and plus-one upper-tail Monte Carlo p for each null. A taxonomic-axis excess is supported only if the observed contrast exceeds the upper 95% interval under both null families.
species_vs_site_axis_contrast.interpretation_boundary: This distinguishes where recruitment is disproportionately allocated; it does not identify the physiological cause of calling.

crossfit_species_shift_plus_persistence_.reason: The cross-fit species-shift null was rejected, but a stronger alternative should jointly allow transferable species-specific rainfall response and strong persistence of each pair's observed dry species x stop state.
crossfit_species_shift_plus_persistence_.species_shifts: Exactly the same deterministic cross-route folds, estimability gate, and per-species training model as crossfit_species_shift_null.
crossfit_species_shift_plus_persistence_.persistence: Cell-only historical dry probabilities anchored 75% to the observed dry matrix, matching the primary persistence-preserving null.
crossfit_species_shift_plus_persistence_.pair_shift: Apply gamma_species * rain_contrast to the anchored logit probabilities, then solve one common pair delta so expected wet incidence count matches the observed wet total.
crossfit_species_shift_plus_persistence_.primary_test: Same four-component Mahalanobis omnibus; plus-one Monte Carlo p.

interpretation.fail_to_reject: Species-specific response heterogeneity plus pair-specific persistence is sufficient under this stronger additive null.
interpretation.reject: Even transferable species-specific response plus strong dry-state persistence is insufficient; additional context dependence or non-additive species x site structure is required.

calling_index_same_observer_sensitivity.reason: CallingIndex levels are observer-scored. Test whether the threshold-recruitment decomposition persists when both surveys in each wetter-drier pair were scored by the same ObserverTrackingID.
calling_index_same_observer_sensitivity.sample: Use the existing prefrozen same-observer restriction: nonempty identical ObserverTrackingID in both runs; expected 3,152 of 4,236 pairs.
calling_index_same_observer_sensitivity.decomposition: Exactly the CallingIndex activation, deactivation, shared-intensity, and total definitions from calling_index_decomposition.
calling_index_same_observer_sensitivity.models: Exactly the same pair-level formula and route-clustered covariance.
calling_index_same_observer_sensitivity.decision: Apply the same threshold-dominant rule as the full sample: total beta >0; activation 95% CI >0; activation >50% of total beta; activation beta > shared-intensity beta.
prohibited: No claim that same-observer restriction eliminates all detection bias.
No edits to the frozen RC11 submission claim based on these exploratory results.
No universal-law wording from NAAMP plus FrogID alone.
No treating missing Australian detection rows as sampled absences without an effort audit.
No retuning gates after endpoint readback.
